index_record.dataset_generation_caption:
The figure presents a comparative architectural diagram illustrating two approaches to chart understanding: (a) the conventional approach and (b) the proposed 'Our approach'. The global layout is divided into two horizontal sections, each representing one method, with a shared input chart on the left and downstream tasks on the right. Both sections are set against a light beige background, with distinct labels at the bottom: '(a) Conventional approach' and '(b) Our approach'.

In section (a), the conventional approach begins with an input chart — a pie chart titled 'Better Approach for the U.S. toward Egypt...' from Pew Research Center, showing percentages for different policy options. This chart is connected via a solid black arrow to a rounded rectangle labeled 'Chart Model', which then feeds into a dashed rectangular box listing four downstream tasks: (1) ChartQA, (2) Chart2text, (3) Chart2table, and (4) OpenCQA. Additionally, an instruction prompt ('Write a summary for this chart.') is shown as a separate rounded rectangle, connected by a dashed green arrow to the 'Chart Model', indicating optional instruction-based input.

Section (b), 'Our approach', mirrors the structure but introduces enhancements. The same input chart is processed through a 'Text Extractor' (represented as a blue square with a white 'A') that extracts textual content from the chart, producing a text string: 'Better Approach for the U.S. toward Egypt..., 23%, DK, 26%, Continue milit...'. This extracted text is combined with the original chart and instruction, forming three inputs: 'Chart', 'Visual Text', and 'Instruction', all enclosed in dashed blue borders. These three inputs are fed into a model labeled 'AskChart' (a gradient-filled rounded rectangle), which then connects to the same set of four downstream tasks as in the conventional approach.

Connections are color-coded: solid black arrows indicate primary data flow; dashed purple arrows link the input chart to both approaches; dashed green arrows denote instruction input; and a dashed blue arrow connects the text extractor output to the 'Visual Text' component in the proposed method. On the far right, two text boxes show sample outputs: the top one, in red text, represents a raw, less coherent response from the conventional approach, while the bottom one, marked with a green check, shows a more fluent and accurate summary generated by the proposed method. The figure visually emphasizes that integrating explicit visual text extraction leads to improved chart understanding performance.
